question: The English East India Company obtained the famous 'Golden Farman' in 1632, which allowed them to trade freely in the ports of Golconda (including Masulipatnam) on a fixed payment. Which ruler issued this farman?
options: The Adil Shahi Sultan of Bijapur
explanation: In 1632, the Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda (Abdullah Qutb Shah) issued the 'Golden Farman' to the English East India Company. This farman allowed them to trade freely in the ports of Golconda, including Masulipatnam, on payment of a fixed duty of 500 pagodas per year.

question: Why was Masulipatnam a highly coveted trading port for European merchant companies in the 17th century?
options: It was the only port producing high-quality spices in South India
It was the main outlet for the celebrated Golconda diamonds and the famous painted/printed cotton textiles (Chintz/Kalamkari)
It was completely free from the control of any local Indian rulers
It was the capital city of the Vijayanagara Empire
explanation: Masulipatnam was the chief port of the kingdom of Golconda. It was famous for Kalamkari textiles (printed and painted cotton cloths) and was a major trading center for diamonds from the Golconda mines, iron, and saltpetre, making it highly valuable to European merchants.
